# Kenneth Loi

> UC Berkeley Biophysics graduate student in the Doudna Lab, focused on molecular primitives, genetic conflict, and computational workflows for biological discovery and design.

## About

Grew up on Frank Herbert, Ted Chiang, and my grandmother's gong sik chaau min under the Southern California Sun.

Probably somewhere flipping rocks.

## Research Themes

- Molecular primitives: looking for biological mechanisms that can become reusable parts: recognition, cutting, sensing, regulation.
- Genetic conflict: parasites, immune systems, and mobile elements are a hotbed of evolutionary innovation.
- Computation for discovery: building workflows to find mechanisms before they are obvious.

## Selected Works

- A noncontiguous code for RNA-guided DNA recognition at the origin of CRISPR-Cas. Science, 2026. Co-first author. https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aei0498
- VIPR RNA-guided DNA recognition by noncontiguous geometric triplex formation. Science, 2026. https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aei3472
- A miniature CRISPR-Cas10 enzyme confers immunity by an inverse signaling pathway. Nature, 2025. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09569-9
- Structure-guided discovery of ancestral CRISPR-Cas13 ribonucleases. Science, 2024. https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adq0553
- Eukaryotic RNA-guided endonucleases evolved from a unique clade of bacterial enzymes. Nucleic Acids Research, 2023. https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/51/22/12414/7424439
